name: Qwen3.6 Plus
description:
Here is how to read the Qwen3.6 Plus config.json. The architecture class is Qwen3ForCausalLM, which is the transformers (or equivalent) module that wires embeddings, attention, the MLP, and the language-modelling head that turns hidden states into next-token logits.

hidden_size is 2,560: that is the width of every residual stream vector. The embedding matrix is therefore 151,936 × 2,560: each token id owns a vector of that width.

num_attention_heads is 32, so each head sees 128 dimensions (2,560 / 32). The ratio test is hidden_size / num_attention_heads = 2560 / 32 = 128. 128 is a multiple of 32 (NVIDIA warp-friendly), and a multiple of 16 (Huawei cube-friendly), and a power of two (Triton / FlashAttention-friendly). From this number alone you cannot name the training chip.

num_key_value_heads is 8, so this is grouped-query attention (GQA): 32 query heads share 8 key/value groups, so the KV cache is about 4× smaller than full MHA.

num_hidden_layers is 36: the stack is that many transformer blocks deep.

intermediate_size is 9,728. In a SwiGLU MLP this is the high-dimensional workspace: the 2,560-wide stream is projected up, activated with silu, then projected back. Labs usually round this width to a multiple of 128 or 256 so it tiles on the chip.

max_position_embeddings is 262,144 tokens — the context window in the config. There is no rope_scaling entry, so the rotary positions are used as-is. rope_theta is 5000000: that is the wavelength of the rotary embedding. A larger theta keeps distant tokens from aliasing after a full rotation.

vocab_size is 151,936. 151,936 is divisible by 128. bos/eos ids, when present, are just two special rows in that table; the padded vocab is often larger than the tokenizer’s real inventory.

tie_word_embeddings is true: the same matrix is reused for input embeddings and the LM head.

torch_dtype is float16.

The copy of config.json is from https://huggingface.co/nhe-ai/Qwen3-4B-Qwen3.6-plus-Reasoning-Distilled-mlx-8Bit/blob/main/config.json.
